notes.provenance: Every numeric value in this file was transcribed from a table or an explicit numeric statement already published in the two source posts. Nothing was re-derived, re-computed, interpolated or estimated. Fields the posts do not publish are null.
notes.provenance_doc: provenance.md (same directory) maps every block to the exact post + table it came from.
notes.rounding: Values are stored exactly as printed in the posts, including their published precision. Where the same quantity is printed twice at different precision (e.g. Sharpe -0.615 in the appendix table vs -0.62 in prose), the table value is stored and the prose value is recorded under discrepancies.
notes.not_re_derived: sd_player_return, bust_rate and a per-overall-pick EV curve are NOT published for most rows. They are left null rather than back-solved. See model.identities for the relationship the board may use if it chooses to derive them itself, explicitly and visibly.
notes.frozen: Both posts are published analyses of 2009/2010-2022 draft classes. Treat this file as a frozen snapshot of what those posts state. Do not edit numbers here to 'improve' them.

units.hit_rate_pct: percent of picks in the bucket that met the snap-based hit threshold
units.p_elite_pct: percent of picks in the bucket whose player return cleared the global elite threshold
units.mean_player_return_cap_frac: mean player return as a FRACTION of the salary cap (0.2176 = 21.76% of cap)
units.fa_replacement_cap_pct: free-agency replacement cost as a PERCENT of the salary cap
units.career_av: Pro Football Reference weighted career Approximate Value
units.surplus_usd_m: surplus value in millions of USD, as published
units.prospect_score: NFL Next Gen Stats composite prospect score, 0-100, published pre-draft

model.name: Quasi-Sharpe ratio for NFL draft picks

formulas.rookie_surplus: Rookie Surplus = Snap Ratio x (FA Replacement Cost - Rookie Salary) x 4 years
formulas.player_return: Player Return = Second Contract Cap% + Rookie Surplus
formulas.sharpe: Sharpe = ( P(elite) x Elite Threshold - FA Replacement Cost ) / SD(Player Return)

identities.sd_from_sharpe: SD(Player Return) = ( P(elite) x Elite Threshold - FA Replacement Cost ) / Sharpe. NOT applied in this file; the two SD values below are the only ones the posts print.
identities.note: The posts publish SD only for QB Top 10 and RB Top 10 (worked example table).

components.computed: snap_ratio x (FA cost - rookie salary) x 4 years
APY as % of salary cap on next deal

components.measures: Cost of buying a starter instead
components.computed: Median of top-N FA contracts/yr; N = avg starter-caliber FAs available per position
Std dev of player returns (including busts at $0)

model.elite_threshold_definition: 90th percentile of all player returns, global across all positions
model.hit_definition: Average snap percentage over the player's first 4 NFL seasons reaches at least 75% of the positional No. 1 starter baseline. Snap % is averaged over ALL expected games (seasons not played count as zero).

sample_window.as_stated_in_draft_sharpe_footer: drafted players 2009-2022 with snap count data available (2013+)
sample_window.as_stated_in_sharpe_counter: 2010-2022 draft classes (minimum 4 NFL seasons for fair evaluation)
sample_window.note: The two posts state slightly different start years. Both statements preserved verbatim; neither reconciled.

model.rookie_surplus_share_note: For most players with positive returns, the rookie contract accounts for 77-95% of the total return (interquartile range).
data_sources_cited: Pro Football Reference (draft picks, snap counts, weighted career AV)
OverTheCap (contracts, normalized to % of salary cap)
NFL Next Gen Stats prospect scores

tiers_note: The five buckets and their labels are published. The numeric pick ranges are NOT published in either post; they are the conventional reading of the labels and are flagged pick_range_published:false. Compensatory picks make rounds 3-7 variable in length year to year. Any board that maps an overall pick to a tier is applying an assumption of its own, not a published one.

gaps: bust_rate is not published for any position or tier in either post. Hit rate is published; the posts never define or print a bust rate. All bust_rate_pct fields are null.
SD(player return) is published only for QB Top 10 (25.7%) and RB Top 10 (9.7%). All other sd_player_return_cap_pct fields are null.
No expected-value-by-overall-pick table exists. The surplus-by-pick curves in post 003 are chart images only. picks.per_overall_pick_curve_published is false.
Tier-to-pick-range mapping is not published; the ranges in tiers[] are conventional readings of the labels and are flagged pick_range_published:false.
FA starter supply per year is printed for OT (3), QB (3) and IOL (8) only. The other eight positions are chart-only and are null.
Best second-contract cap% is printed only for RB (~8%) and WR (~14%), both as approximations. Null elsewhere.
The career-AV Sharpe variant publishes only RB (0.249, 6th of 11). The other ten positions' values are null.
2026 class Good+ counts are printed for CB (34), WR (32), IOL (31), RB (8) and QB (10) only. The remaining six positions are null.
Per-year class-depth counts by position exist only in charts; only a handful of RB years are stated in text.
The Top 10 / Round 1 surplus leaderboards and all Top-5-by-position appendices are images. Their player rows and values are not in the HTML and are absent here.
Team-level draft-efficiency scores are published for PHI (+0.24) and PIT (-0.64) only; the full 32-team ranking is chart-only.
Athlete Score and Size Score are not published for any individual prospect (only Love's Production Score, 95.9).
Rookie wage-scale APY by pick (a CBA input the models use) is never tabulated in either post.
Elite-threshold equivalents in dollars, and the cap value used to convert cap% to $M, are never published - so cap% and $M figures here cannot be converted into each other.
